title: Lady Bird Deed States and Transfer on Death Deeds by State (2026)
subtitle: Which states recognize the lady bird deed, which have a TOD or beneficiary deed statute, 50 states and DC
description:
For each of the 50 US states and the District of Columbia, this dataset records whether a lady bird deed (enhanced life estate deed) has primary legal authority and of what kind (statute, court decision, Medicaid agency rule, or a court that declined it), whether a transfer on death or beneficiary deed statute exists with its citation, effective date and uniform-act status, what the instrument is called there, which instrument an owner there would use, and whether Medicaid estate recovery can reach a home passed by each deed.

Seven states have authority for the lady bird deed (Rhode Island and Vermont by statute; Florida, Maryland, Michigan and Texas by court decision; North Carolina only in its Medicaid manual), Iowa's Court of Appeals has said the state does not recognize it, 34 states plus DC have a transfer on death deed statute, and 11 states have neither. All court decisions were re-checked on October 7, 2026 against a search of every court in the CourtListener corpus. Column definitions are in schema.json.
